settings.source: TABLE: Body temperature, YELLOW ('7-day baseline'). Applied to all rolling baselines = ASSUMPTION A3 in specs/rules-engine.md

escalation.source: TABLE: column headers H ('YELLOW - crew should act') and I ('RED - ground flight surgeon needed'); BRIEF §4

ui_text.baseline_forming: Your personal baseline is still forming. Only general limits are checked for now.
ui_text.escalation_self: No action needed. Keep your routine.
ui_text.escalation_ground_flight_surgeon: Contact the flight surgeon on Earth. Tell your crew medical officer now.

flags.label: Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Sweating, shakiness, sudden hunger, unusual fatigue or dizziness
Vomiting, dehydration, abdominal pain or excessive thirst
Seizure or loss of consciousness (crewmate reports)
During exercise: dizziness, confusion or sweating stops
I made task errors because of fatigue
Stress, sadness, loneliness or irritability on most recent days
Severe anxiety, panic or rapidly worsening distress
I feel unable to do my mission tasks safely
Swelling of the face or throat
New itching, dryness, redness or mild swelling
A small wound has not improved in 48 hours
New or changing mole or dark spot
Redness, warmth or swelling that spreads quickly
Pus or red streaks around a wound
My dosimeter shows unexpectedly high exposure

rules.source: TABLE: Blood pressure, YELLOW
rules.title: Blood pressure higher than usual
rules.explanation: Your systolic pressure was 130 mmHg or higher on repeated readings. In microgravity, fluid shifts change how your heart and vessels work.
actions: Rest for 5 minutes and measure again.
Note any dizziness, headache or unusual weakness.
Tell your crew medical officer if it stays high.

rules.source: TABLE: Blood pressure, YELLOW
rules.title: Blood pressure higher than usual
rules.explanation: Your diastolic pressure was 80 mmHg or higher on repeated readings.
actions: Rest for 5 minutes and measure again.
Note any dizziness, headache or unusual weakness.
Tell your crew medical officer if it stays high.

rules.source: TABLE: Blood pressure, YELLOW
rules.title: Blood pressure lower than usual
rules.explanation: Your systolic pressure was below 90 mmHg on repeated readings. Low pressure can cause dizziness and fainting.
actions: Rest for 5 minutes and measure again.
Note any dizziness or weakness.
Tell your crew medical officer if it stays low.

rules.source: TABLE: Blood pressure, YELLOW
rules.title: Blood pressure lower than usual
rules.explanation: Your diastolic pressure was below 60 mmHg on repeated readings.
actions: Rest for 5 minutes and measure again.
Note any dizziness or weakness.
Tell your crew medical officer if it stays low.

rules.source: TABLE: Blood pressure, YELLOW ('persistent deviation from individual baseline'); 10 mmHg [ANSWER: Lana, 14 Nov 13:36, '9-10 mmHg'] - SOURCE PENDING (PubMed, Ayesha); 2 consecutive days (A2)
rules.title: Blood pressure differs from your normal
rules.explanation: Your blood pressure has been at least 10 mmHg away from your personal normal for 2 days.
actions: Measure again after 5 minutes of rest.
Tell your crew medical officer if it continues.

rules.source: TABLE: Blood pressure, YELLOW ('persistent deviation from individual baseline'); 10 mmHg [ANSWER: Lana, 14 Nov 13:36, '9-10 mmHg'] - SOURCE PENDING (PubMed, Ayesha); 2 consecutive days (A2)
rules.title: Blood pressure differs from your normal
rules.explanation: Your blood pressure has been at least 10 mmHg away from your personal normal for 2 days.
actions: Measure again after 5 minutes of rest.
Tell your crew medical officer if it continues.

rules.source: TABLE: Blood pressure, RED
rules.title: Very high blood pressure
rules.explanation: Your systolic pressure reached 180 mmHg or higher. This needs medical assessment now.
actions: Measure again now if you feel able.
Start the approved medical emergency procedure.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.

rules.source: TABLE: Blood pressure, RED
rules.title: Very high blood pressure
rules.explanation: Your diastolic pressure reached 120 mmHg or higher. This needs medical assessment now.
actions: Measure again now if you feel able.
Start the approved medical emergency procedure.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.

rules.source: TABLE: Blood pressure, RED ('very low BP with fainting or severe dizziness'). 'Very low' = below the YELLOW low limit: ASSUMPTION A5.
rules.title: Low blood pressure with fainting or severe dizziness
rules.explanation: Low blood pressure together with fainting or severe dizziness can mean your circulation is unstable.
actions: Lie down and secure yourself.
Call your crew medical officer now.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.
rules.recheck: Repeat as soon as it is safe.

rules.source: TABLE: Heart rate, YELLOW ('persistent deviation from individual baseline'); deviation 12 bpm [ANSWER: Lana, 14 Nov 13:36] - SOURCE PENDING (Ayesha); 'persistent' = 2 consecutive days (A2)
rules.title: Heart rate differs from your normal
rules.explanation: Your resting heart rate has been at least 12 beats per minute away from your personal normal for 2 days. Your heart adapts to microgravity, so a change from YOUR usual value matters even inside general limits.
actions: Sit still for 5 minutes and measure again.
Note chest pain, dizziness or shortness of breath.
Tell your crew medical officer if it continues.
rules.recheck: Repeat after 5 minutes of rest and again tomorrow morning.

rules.source: TABLE: Heart rate, Normal range (60-100 bpm, added by team 14 Nov) - SOURCE LINK PENDING (Ayesha)
rules.title: Resting heart rate above 100
rules.explanation: Your resting heart rate is above the general adult range of 60-100 beats per minute.
actions: Sit still for 5 minutes and measure again.
Note chest pain, dizziness or shortness of breath.
Tell your crew medical officer if it continues.

rules.source: TABLE: Heart rate, Normal range (60-100 bpm, added by team 14 Nov) - SOURCE LINK PENDING (Ayesha)
rules.title: Resting heart rate below 60
rules.explanation: Your resting heart rate is below the general adult range of 60-100 beats per minute.
actions: Sit still for 5 minutes and measure again.
Note chest pain, dizziness or shortness of breath.
Tell your crew medical officer if it continues.

rules.source: TABLE: Heart rate, RED ('abnormal heart rate with chest pain, fainting, severe dizziness or shortness of breath'); deviation 12 bpm [ANSWER: Lana] - SOURCE PENDING (Ayesha)
rules.title: Unusual heart rate with warning symptoms
rules.explanation: An unusual heart rate together with chest pain, fainting, severe dizziness or shortness of breath needs medical assessment now.
actions: Stop all activity and secure yourself.
Call your crew medical officer now.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.

rules.source: TABLE: Heart rate, RED ('suspected arrhythmia or irregular heart rhythm')
rules.title: Possible irregular heartbeat
rules.explanation: An irregular heartbeat needs to be checked by a doctor.
actions: Stop strenuous activity.
Tell your crew medical officer now.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.

rules.source: TABLE: Blood sugar, YELLOW
rules.title: Low blood sugar
rules.explanation: Your glucose is below 70 mg/dL. Low sugar can affect energy and concentration.
actions: Stop strenuous activity.
If you can swallow, take fast-acting glucose as in the approved protocol.
Tell your crew medical officer if it stays low.

rules.source: TABLE: Blood sugar, YELLOW
rules.title: High blood sugar
rules.explanation: Your glucose stayed above 180 mg/dL on repeated readings, not just after a meal. Long spaceflight can change how your body uses sugar.
actions: Confirm the reading with a finger-prick test if you can.
Tell your crew medical officer if it stays high.
rules.recheck: Recheck at the next scheduled measurement.

rules.source: TABLE: Blood sugar, YELLOW
rules.title: Symptoms of low blood sugar
rules.explanation: Sweating, shakiness, sudden hunger or dizziness can be signs of low blood sugar.
actions: Stop strenuous activity and measure your glucose.
Tell your crew medical officer if symptoms continue.

rules.source: TABLE: Blood sugar, RED
rules.title: Very low blood sugar
rules.explanation: Your glucose is below 54 mg/dL. This is clinically significant low blood sugar.
actions: If you can swallow, take fast-acting glucose now.
Start the approved emergency procedure.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.

rules.source: TABLE: Blood sugar, RED ('regardless of the measured glucose level')
rules.title: Confusion or loss of consciousness
rules.explanation: Confusion, seizures or loss of consciousness need help right away, whatever the glucose value.
actions: A crewmate starts the approved emergency procedure.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.
rules.recheck: Measure glucose as soon as it is safe.

rules.source: TABLE: Blood sugar, RED ('persistently above 200 mg/dL with symptoms or suspected ketones')
rules.title: High blood sugar with symptoms
rules.explanation: Glucose above 200 mg/dL with symptoms or ketones can mean a high-sugar crisis.
actions: Check ketones if available.
Start the approved emergency procedure.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.

rules.source: TABLE: Blood sugar, RED ('vomiting, dehydration, abdominal pain, excessive thirst ... suggest a possible hyperglycemic crisis')
rules.title: Possible high-sugar crisis
rules.explanation: Vomiting, dehydration, belly pain or strong thirst can be signs of a high-sugar crisis.
actions: Measure your glucose now.
Tell your crew medical officer.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.

rules.source: TABLE: Body temperature, YELLOW ('at least 1 °C above the astronaut's own 7-day baseline')
rules.title: Temperature above your normal
rules.explanation: Your resting temperature is at least 1 °C above your own 7-day average. In space, resting temperature runs higher than on Earth, so we compare with your normal.
actions: Rest and drink water.
Lower exercise intensity and take cooling breaks.
Tell your crew medical officer if it stays high.

rules.source: TABLE: Body temperature, YELLOW ('37.8 to 38.9 °C'). DISABLED pending OPEN QUESTION Q-TEMP: conflicts with TABLE: Body temperature, Normal ('in-flight resting core may stabilise near 38 °C').
rules.title: Raised temperature
rules.explanation: Your resting temperature is 37.8 °C or higher.
actions: Rest and drink water.
Tell your crew medical officer if it stays high.

rules.source: TABLE: Body temperature, YELLOW
rules.title: Temperature lower than normal
rules.explanation: Your resting temperature is below 36.0 °C.
actions: Check that the sensor is placed correctly.
Warm up and measure again.
Tell your crew medical officer if it stays low.

rules.source: TABLE: Body temperature, YELLOW ('core temperature after exercise is 39.0 °C or higher')
rules.title: Overheating after exercise
rules.explanation: Your temperature after exercise reached 39.0 °C. In microgravity your body loses heat less easily.
actions: Stop or reduce exercise.
Take a cooling break, increase airflow, drink water.

rules.source: TABLE: Body temperature, RED
rules.title: High fever
rules.explanation: Your resting temperature is 39.0 °C or higher.
actions: Rest and drink water.
Tell your crew medical officer now.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth. Take fever medicine only on their advice.

rules.source: TABLE: Body temperature, RED ('at least 1 °C above baseline for more than 24 hours'). '>24 h' = 2 consecutive daily readings: ASSUMPTION A4.
rules.title: Temperature above your normal for more than a day
rules.explanation: Your temperature has stayed at least 1 °C above your normal for more than a day.
actions: Tell your crew medical officer now.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.

rules.source: TABLE: Body temperature, RED ('fever with chills, confusion, severe headache, rash or breathing difficulty'). Fever = YELLOW baseline rule: ASSUMPTION A6.
rules.title: Fever with warning symptoms
rules.explanation: A raised temperature together with chills, confusion, severe headache, rash or breathing difficulty needs a doctor.
actions: Tell your crew medical officer now.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.

rules.source: TABLE: Body temperature, RED
rules.title: Very low temperature
rules.explanation: Your temperature is below 35.0 °C.
actions: Warm up and check the sensor.
Tell your crew medical officer now.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.

rules.source: TABLE: Body temperature, RED ('during exercise or spacewalks: 40.0 °C or higher')
rules.title: Dangerous overheating
rules.explanation: Your temperature during exercise reached 40.0 °C or higher.
actions: Stop exercising now and cool down.
Tell your crew medical officer now.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.

rules.source: TABLE: Body temperature, RED ('dizziness, confusion or sweating that stops' during exercise)
rules.title: Signs of heat stress
rules.explanation: Dizziness, confusion or sweating that stops during exercise are signs of dangerous heat stress.
actions: Stop exercising now and cool down.
Tell your crew medical officer now.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.

rules.source: TABLE: Sleep hours, YELLOW
rules.title: Not enough sleep this week
rules.explanation: Your 7-day average sleep is below 7 hours. Short sleep raises the risk of errors and lowers mood and immunity.
actions: Review your schedule and protect your sleep window.
Keep the sleep area dark, quiet and cool.
Log your sleep every day.

rules.source: TABLE: Sleep hours, YELLOW ('any use of sleep aids')
rules.title: Sleep aid used
rules.explanation: Using a sleep aid is worth discussing with your crew medical officer.
actions: Tell your crew medical officer.
Use sleep medicine only with flight surgeon guidance.

rules.source: TABLE: Sleep hours, RED ('6 hours or less per night for 7 nights in a row')
rules.title: A week of short sleep
rules.explanation: You slept 6 hours or less for 7 nights in a row.
actions: Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.
Reduce critical tasks until rested, if possible.

rules.source: TABLE: Sleep hours, RED ('errors during tasks caused by fatigue')
rules.title: Fatigue is causing errors
rules.explanation: Errors caused by fatigue are a safety risk for you and the crew.
actions: Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.
Reduce critical tasks until rested, if possible.

rules.source: TABLE: Mood, YELLOW ('decrease of 2 or more points from personal baseline for 3 consecutive days'); baseline = preflight per TABLE: Mood, Normal
rules.title: Mood lower than your usual
rules.explanation: Your mood has been 2 or more points below your usual for 3 days. Isolation and distance from home can affect mood.
actions: Take a moment to review what changed recently.
Talk with a crewmate or contact family.
Keep regular sleep and exercise.
Contact your crew medical officer if it continues.

rules.source: TABLE: Mood, YELLOW ('repeatedly reports increased stress, sadness, loneliness or irritability')
rules.title: You have been feeling low
rules.explanation: Stress, sadness, loneliness or irritability on most days is worth paying attention to.
actions: Talk with a crewmate or contact family.
Try a relaxation exercise.
Contact your crew medical officer if it continues.

rules.source: TABLE: Mood, RED
rules.title: You deserve support right now
rules.explanation: What you are feeling matters. You do not have to handle it alone.
actions: Talk to your crew medical officer now.
Send a private message to the flight surgeon and behavioral health support on Earth.
rules.recheck: Stay with a crewmate if you can.

rules.source: TABLE: Body mass, YELLOW ('sustained decrease of approximately 2% or more from preflight baseline'). 'Sustained' = 2 consecutive readings: ASSUMPTION A2.
rules.title: Body mass going down
rules.explanation: Your body mass is at least 2% below your preflight value. Losing mass can mean you are not eating enough and losing muscle or bone.
actions: Measure again.
Review your food and fluid intake and your exercise.
Tell your crew medical officer if it continues.
rules.recheck: Measure again at the next scheduled check.

rules.source: TABLE: Body mass, RED ('loss of approximately 5% or more accompanied by ... weakness, dizziness')
rules.title: Large body mass loss with symptoms
rules.explanation: You have lost 5% or more of your body mass and feel weak or dizzy.
actions: Tell your crew medical officer.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth for assessment.
rules.recheck: Measure again at the next scheduled check.

rules.source: TABLE: Immune signs / symptoms, YELLOW
rules.title: New mild symptoms
rules.explanation: Spaceflight can weaken the immune system and wake up dormant viruses, so new symptoms are worth tracking.
actions: Record your symptoms and measure your temperature.
Follow hygiene precautions.
Tell your crew medical officer.

rules.source: TABLE: Immune signs / symptoms, RED
rules.title: Serious symptoms
rules.explanation: These symptoms need medical assessment right away.
actions: Tell your crew medical officer now.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.

rules.source: TABLE: Immune signs / symptoms, RED ('38 °C or higher with other infection symptoms'). DISABLED pending OPEN QUESTION Q-TEMP: conflicts with TABLE: Body temperature, RED (39.0 °C).
rules.title: Fever with signs of infection
rules.explanation: A temperature of 38 °C or higher with infection symptoms needs a doctor.
actions: Tell your crew medical officer now.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.
rules.recheck: Measure your temperature again in 30 minutes.

rules.source: TABLE: Radiation dose, YELLOW ('dose rate rises above the expected mission baseline'). ILLUSTRATIVE MISSION SETTING (Q-RAD, 15 Nov 2026, Mars transit): expected cruise rate ≈ 75 µSv/h (MSL/RAD, Zeitlin et al., Science 2013: ≈ 1.8 mSv/day); yellow above 2 × expected = 150 µSv/h. Not a medical limit.
rules.title: Radiation higher than expected
rules.explanation: The dose rate is above what is expected for this mission.
actions: Check your personal dosimeter.
Follow radiation alerts and move to the shielded area when instructed.
rules.recheck: Check the dosimeter again in 1 hour.

rules.source: TABLE: Radiation dose, YELLOW ('a solar particle event warning is issued')
rules.title: Solar particle event warning
rules.explanation: A solar storm can raise radiation levels quickly. Outside Earth's magnetic field you have less natural protection.
actions: Check your personal dosimeter.
Move to the shielded area when instructed.
Wait for instructions from mission control.
rules.recheck: Check the dosimeter after the event.

rules.source: TABLE: Radiation dose, YELLOW ('approaches the mission-specific action level'). ILLUSTRATIVE MISSION SETTING (Q-RAD, 15 Nov 2026, Mars transit): action level = 80 % of the NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 Rev. C (2023): career effective dose limit 600 mSv → 480 mSv. A nominal 180-day transit at ≈ 1.8 mSv/day gives ≈ 324 mSv.
rules.title: Accumulated dose approaching the mission limit
rules.explanation: Your total radiation dose is close to this mission's action level.
actions: Reduce unnecessary exposure.
Tell your crew medical officer.

rules.source: TABLE: Radiation dose, RED ('reaches or exceeds a predefined mission-specific emergency threshold'). ILLUSTRATIVE MISSION SETTING (Q-RAD, 15 Nov 2026, Mars transit): NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 Rev. C (2023): career effective dose limit 600 mSv.
rules.title: Accumulated dose at the emergency limit
rules.explanation: Your total radiation dose has reached this mission's emergency threshold.
actions: Notify mission control and the flight surgeon on Earth now.
Follow radiation protection instructions.

rules.source: TABLE: Radiation dose, RED
rules.title: High radiation exposure
rules.explanation: An unexpectedly high exposure or an acute radiation event needs medical evaluation.
actions: Notify mission control and the flight surgeon on Earth now.
Follow radiation protection instructions.
Note any symptoms such as nausea or skin redness.

rules.source: TABLE: Skin health, YELLOW ('symptom severity reaches 4/10 or higher')
rules.title: Skin symptoms bothering you
rules.explanation: Your skin symptoms are 4 out of 10 or higher. Dry cabin air and limited hygiene can irritate the skin.
actions: Photograph the area to track changes.
Use moisturiser and avoid scratching.
Tell your crew medical officer.

rules.source: TABLE: Skin health, YELLOW
rules.title: New skin change
rules.explanation: New skin changes and slow-healing wounds are worth tracking in space.
actions: Photograph the area to track changes.
Keep minor wounds clean and covered.
Tell your crew medical officer.

rules.source: TABLE: Skin health, RED
rules.title: Possible serious skin infection or reaction
rules.explanation: These signs can mean a serious infection or allergic reaction.
actions: Tell your crew medical officer now.
Contact the flight surgeon on Earth.
rules.recheck: Check the area again in a few hours.
